kaigo-completeness-measurement-context.heading: Report time, site and circumstances with measurements
paragraphs: Vital signs are information about bodily functions, including temperature and pulse. Record measurement time, site, device or method and known circumstances along with the value. Preserve numbers and units accurately without guessing missing conditions. The recipient needs to understand when and under what conditions the value was obtained.

Temperature may be measured at the armpit, ear or forehead with different devices. Two values from different sites or methods cannot be treated as a change under identical conditions. Retain original records and check each set of circumstances. However, differing conditions do not justify ignoring a higher value or the person feeling unwell.

Consider vital signs together with personal words, observations and changes from usual. “I am tired” and a measured value are both needed. One value not being high does not establish that overall health is problem-free. Distinguish unchecked items from items checked without abnormalities.

Breathing, pulse and blood pressure vary with activity and physical or emotional state. Posture also affects blood-pressure measurement. Known circumstances, such as immediately after activity, help interpret change but do not establish its cause. Do not conclude activity or age is responsible; report observations separately from unknowns.

Measure according to device instructions, confirmed individual support, facility procedures and assigned responsibilities. Forehead devices especially require checking their specific operating conditions. This text does not authorize independent fever thresholds, remeasurement times or counts, or treatment methods. Ask the responsible nursing staff or another appropriate person if methods or judgments are unclear.

Report concerns to the facility’s designated recipient with values, measurement conditions, complaints, observations and unchecked items. In urgent situations, immediately request help and follow emergency procedures instead of prioritizing finished records. You can communicate established facts before knowing a cause or diagnosis.

[Learning situation] At 08:00 temperature was measured under the arm; at 15:30 a different device measured the forehead after the person returned from activity. They said, “I am tired.” Separate both measurement conditions and convey their words and the unchecked pulse and breathing. Do not conclude fever, cause or overall health from two values alone; organize information to share the change with the person responsible.

176.title: Report time, site and circumstances with measurements
objectives: Explain conditions needed to understand a measured value.
Report personal words, observed facts and unchecked items separately.
176.context: Learn to communicate values with circumstances by comparing temperatures obtained under different conditions.
176.artCaption: A care worker records while speaking with the person. A blood-pressure cuff is visible on the arm.

weekly-kaigo-completeness-measurement-co.prompt: Which record and handoff are appropriate?
options: Record the higher 15:30 value as caused by activity and omit tiredness as irrelevant.
Treat both values as measured under identical conditions and diagnose fever from the increase alone.
Record each time, site and device, recent activity, personal words and unchecked pulse/breathing separately, and report the change.
Different conditions make comparison unusable, so withhold the higher value and tiredness.
rationales: Recent activity is known but does not establish cause. Tiredness must be communicated with values.
Sites and devices differ, so conditions cannot be treated as identical. Convey circumstances and condition without diagnosing fever from this alone.
Separating conditions, words and unknowns helps the receiver understand and share a concern without assuming cause or diagnosis.
Checking differing conditions does not mean withholding change. Report the higher value and tiredness with established information.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-measurement-co.reading: The 08:00 temperature record used the armpit. At 15:30 another care worker measured the forehead with a different device after activity and recorded only “the new value is higher.” The person says, “I am tired.” Pulse and breathing have not been checked.
